issues.title: Inverted conditional logic in setUserFeatureState causes wrong branch execution
issues.description: The conditional check for handling the 'inherit' state has been inverted from `if (state === 'inherit')` to `if (state !== 'inherit')`. This causes the method to incorrectly pass the state without assignedBy when state is 'enabled' or 'disabled', and incorrectly attempts to access assignedBy property (which doesn't exist in the union type) when state is 'inherit', leading to runtime TypeScript errors and incorrect database operations. When users try to enable/disable a feature, the assignedBy tracking will be lost, and when they set it to inherit, the code will crash trying to access a non-existent property.

issues.title: Missing await in setUserState mutation causes race condition
issues.description: The await keyword was removed from the featureOptInService.setUserFeatureState call in the tRPC mutation handler. This causes the mutation to return success immediately without waiting for the database operation to complete, creating a race condition where the response is sent before the state is actually persisted. Users will receive success responses even if the underlying operation fails, and subsequent reads might not reflect the changes they just made, leading to inconsistent UI state and data integrity issues.

issues.title: Inverted filter logic in listFeaturesForUser returns disabled features instead of enabled
issues.description: The filter condition in listFeaturesForUser was changed from `filter((state) => state.globalEnabled)` to `filter((state) => !state.globalEnabled)`, inverting the logic. This causes the method to return only globally disabled features instead of enabled ones. Users will see an empty or incorrect list of available features in their settings UI, as only features that are globally disabled (which should be hidden) will be shown, while actually available features will be filtered out. This breaks the entire feature opt-in UI for users.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26801 - feat: add scope configuration for feature opt-in

structured_output.summary: The PR adds an optional `scope` field (org/team/user) to opt-in feature config, helpers to filter features by scope, scope validation in `setTeamFeatureState`/`setUserFeatureState`, scope-specific menu visibility constants, and unit tests. The scoping idea and the menu-visibility wiring are reasonable. However, the diff has three functional regressions that would ship broken behavior once any feature is configured: `setUserFeatureState` has its enabled/inherit branches inverted so enable/disable writes omit `assignedBy`, `listFeaturesForUser` inverts its `globalEnabled` filter, and the user-state tRPC mutation drops `await`, so scope errors and write failures are silently lost. The unit tests also mock away the scope filtering they are meant to cover, so they pass against the broken `listFeaturesForTeam` and cannot catch these regressions. A stray debug constant is committed as well.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Three correctness regressions block merge: the inverted `setUserFeatureState` branch breaks enable/disable for users (the repository's upsert reads `input.assignedBy`, which is now undefined), the `listFeaturesForUser` filter is inverted so it shows disabled features and hides enabled ones, and the missing `await` in the user mutation makes scope errors and DB failures invisible to the client. The test suite does not catch any of these, and the existing enabled/inherit assertions in the new tests would fail against this code.

architecture.overview:
Opt-in features are declared in `OPT_IN_FEATURES` (packages/features/feature-opt-in/config.ts). `FeatureOptInService` reads that config and delegates persistence to `FeaturesRepository`, which writes `UserFeatures` and `TeamFeatures` rows through Prisma. The tRPC `featureOptIn` router exposes list and mutation endpoints for the user, team, and org settings pages, and `SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx` decides whether the Features tab appears in the sidebar.

This PR adds a `scope` array to each config entry. Helpers in config.ts (`getOptInFeaturesForScope`, `isFeatureAllowedForScope`) and the new `HAS_*_OPT_IN_FEATURES` flags become the single source for scope decisions. The service uses them to filter list results and to reject mutations for out-of-scope features, and the router passes an explicit scope (`team` or `org`) for each endpoint. The menu now checks scope-specific flags instead of one global flag.
steps: Entry point: the settings pages call tRPC `featureOptIn` routes (`listForTeam`, `listForOrganization`, `setUserState`, `setTeamState`, `setOrganizationState`) in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/featureOptIn/_router.ts`.
Config layer: `OPT_IN_FEATURES` in `packages/features/feature-opt-in/config.ts` gains an optional `scope`. The new helpers and `HAS_*` flags read it, with a missing `scope` meaning all scopes.

Service layer: `FeatureOptInService` filters reads by scope (`listFeaturesForTeam`, `listFeaturesForUser`) and validates scope before writing (`setUserFeatureState`, `setTeamFeatureState`). Both writes reject with `ErrorWithCode(BadRequest)`.

Persistence: the service delegates to `FeaturesRepository.setUserFeatureState` / `setTeamFeatureState`, which upsert `enabled`/`assignedBy` for enabled/disabled and clear rows for inherit. This PR changes the branch logic that picks which call shape to use.
UI: `SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx` shows the user, org, and team Features tabs only when the matching `HAS_*_OPT_IN_FEATURES` flag is true.

findings.title: setUserFeatureState branches inverted: enable/disable writes lose assignedBy
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/feature-opt-in/services/FeatureOptInService.ts`, `setUserFeatureState` (around lines 264-274) has its branches inverted. The condition was changed to `state !== "inherit"`, so enabled/disabled calls drop `assignedBy`, which `FeaturesRepository.setUserFeatureState` needs for upsert. Restore the original structure: `if (state === "inherit")` calls the repository with `{ userId, featureId, state }`, and the else branch passes `assignedBy: \`user-${assignedBy}\``. Keep the scope check above it unchanged. Then confirm the enabled, disabled, and inherit assertions in `FeatureOptInService.test.ts` pass.

findings.title: listFeaturesForUser filter inverted, so disabled features are returned
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/feature-opt-in/services/FeatureOptInService.ts` at line 207, `listFeaturesForUser` filters with `!state.globalEnabled`, which is inverted. Change it back to `.filter((state) => state.globalEnabled)` to match the doc comment ("globally enabled") and the `listFeaturesForTeam` filter. Add a unit test for `listFeaturesForUser` that checks a globally disabled feature is excluded and an enabled one is returned.

findings.title: Missing await on user-state mutation swallows scope errors and write failures
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/featureOptIn/_router.ts`, the `setUserState` mutation (around line 103) calls `featureOptInService.setUserFeatureState(...)` without `await`. Add `await` so scope validation errors and repository failures propagate to the client, matching `setTeamState` and `setOrganizationState` in the same file.

findings.title: Unit tests mock the scope helpers, so the scope filtering they claim to cover is never exercised
findings.body:
The test file mocks `getOptInFeaturesForScope` as `() => mockFeatures`. The mock ignores its argument, so every call returns all five features. This has two effects:

- The `listFeaturesForTeam` tests assert that `getTeamsFeatureStates` is called with all five feature IDs, including `org-only-feature` and `user-only-feature`, when a team-scoped query should only include `team-only-feature` and unscoped features. The test encodes the wrong behavior and passes only because of the mock.
- `isFeatureAllowedForScope` is also mocked, so none of the real scope logic in config.ts is tested. The validation tests just flip `mockIsFeatureAllowedForScope`, which tests the mock, not the function.

The PR description says 16 tests cover scope validation edge cases, but the missing behavior is exactly the scope-filtering logic. None of the tests cover the real `getOptInFeaturesForScope` or `isFeatureAllowedForScope`, and nothing covers `HAS_*_OPT_IN_FEATURES`.

::diff{file="packages/features/feature-opt-in/services/FeatureOptInService.test.ts" lines="16-29"}

Suggested direction: test the real config helpers in a separate `config.test.ts` (scoped features, unscoped defaults to all, unknown slug returns false). In the service tests, make `getOptInFeaturesForScope` use the real filter, or keep the mock but assert the team query contains only team-scoped and unscoped features.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/feature-opt-in/services/FeatureOptInService.test.ts`, the `vi.mock("../config")` block (lines ~16-29) replaces `getOptInFeaturesForScope` with `() => mockFeatures`, which ignores scope, and also mocks `isFeatureAllowedForScope`. As a result the `listFeaturesForTeam` expectations (around lines 84, 119, 198) assert all five feature IDs are queried, which is the wrong scoped behavior. Change the mock so the scope filter is applied (or use the real helper) and update those expectations to the team-scoped subset (`test-feature-1`, `test-feature-2`, `team-only-feature`). Add a new `config.test.ts` that tests `getOptInFeaturesForScope`, `isFeatureAllowedForScope`, and the `HAS_*_OPT_IN_FEATURES` flags against a fixture list. Add a `listFeaturesForUser` test as well.
